misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component that invokes the VM, part of the internal transaction processing pipeline, not an external entity
Output target receiving data FROM the system, not an input source sending data INTO the system
Output target receiving transaction announcements, not an input source

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain (Consensus Layer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Consensus layer provides withdrawal requests via Engine API. JWT authenticated communication but withdrawal data structure must still be validated. Trust derives from authenticated interface, not blind trust of content.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peer transmitting block headers and data. Peers are untrusted by default; full validation of parent hash, state root, transaction root, receipt root, withdrawals root, blob gas fields, and beacon root required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Announcing Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer sending eth/68 NewPooledTransactionHashes announcements. Peers may provide inaccurate type and size metadata. Receiving nodes should implement throttling and not blindly trust announced sizes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled malicious actor attempting bandwidth exhaustion via large transactions. Represents adversarial input for security analysis. All inputs from this entity require maximum scrutiny.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application or user submitting transactions via JSON-RPC interface. No authentication required for public RPC endpoints. Timeout parameters must be validated, transaction data must pass format validation.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Engine API JWT authentication provides channel security. Withdrawal fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) must be validated for correct types (U64, U64, Address, U256).

Full header validation required: parent_hash, ommers_hash (must equal EMPTY_OMMER_HASH), state_root, transactions_root, receipt_root, withdrawals_root, blob_gas_used, excess_blob_gas, parent_beacon_block_root.

Type and size metadata in eth/68 announcements should be used for bandwidth budget decisions but not trusted implicitly. Peers lying about size can still be detected when actual transaction is fetched.
Bandwidth throttling policies must be applied based on announced size. Per-peer and global limits prevent amplification attacks. Peer behavior tracking enables reputation-based throttling.

Timeout parameter must be validated as positive integer not exceeding node-configured maximum. Transaction data must pass standard eth_sendRawTransaction format validation. Nodes must implement reasonable timeout maximums to prevent resource exhaustion.
Invalid timeout values should fall back to node default (recommended 2 seconds). Invalid transaction data returns JSON-RPC error. Synchronous wait must not block critical node operations.
